result:
I fixed 12 rules in `pricebook.py`. A check script parsed each docstring and compared the rule with what the docstring describes across many qty/unit combinations. All 150 rules now match.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 07, 32, 140 | Labeled marginal, but computed the discount on the full amount | Discount now applies only to units above the threshold |
| 47 | Labeled whole, but computed the discount marginally | Discount now applies to the full amount |
| 14 | Used 13% (docstring says 12%) | Changed to 12% |
| 131 | Used 16% (docstring says 15%) | Changed to 15% |
| 56 | Threshold was 6 (docstring says 5) | Changed to `qty >= 5` |
| 39 | Capped the amount the percentage is taken from, not the discount itself | Discount is calculated first, then capped |
| 72 | Capped only when the discount was over 20,000 won | Discount is always capped at 10,000 won |
| 85, 90 | Rounded the discount instead of flooring it | Changed to `// 100` |
| 121 | Used `qty > 5` | Changed to `qty >= 5` for consistency. Results don't change, because the marginal discount at exactly 5 units is 0 |

STATUS: DONE
